(3) "For a two-component oriented link diagram D = D_1 ∪ D_2 with linking number lk, [z^{-1}] H_D = (a − a⁻¹) a^{−2 lk} [z^0](H_{D_1} H_{D_2})" (excerpt 3-5) -> two_component_row (stmt 458-461). D : Diagram with componentCount = 2, i ≠ j (so {i, j} is the whole component set); D_1, D_2 = D.knotRestrict i/j := D.restrict {i} (stmt 192-193; knotRestrict_componentCount 197-201), the "actual knot restrictions" of mp:lowest 1584 which the proof names "Its two intrinsic restrictions are the actual diagrams D_1, D_2" (excerpt 26). lk: the proof fixes it as "Its linking half-sum computed from the original common presentation, with the crossing signs of def:positive-lift, exactly the lk in the statement" (excerpt 22-25), i.e. lk = ℓ_12 = ½ Σ σ(x) over ALL mixed crossings (mp:lowest 1585-1586). twoLinking D i j := mixedSignSum D i j (stmt 210; ZeroLink.lean:31-34) = Σ over ordered strand pairs (s on i, t on j) forming a crossing of D.sign ⟨{s,t},_⟩ (sign = sgn det(u_over, u_under), LinkDiagram.lean:552); for i ≠ j each mixed crossing contributes exactly one term (the pair (t, s) fails s.1 = i), so twoLinking = Σ σ(x) = 2 lk and aPow (−(twoLinking D i j)) = LaurentPolynomial.T (−2 lk) = a^{−2 lk} (stmt 117). No division is used, as the proof stresses (excerpt 34-35). (a − a⁻¹) = aPow 1 − aPow (−1) in ℤ[a^{±1}]; [z^k] = zRow k (LinkLaurentRing.lean:335, pinned by coeff_zRow 338: coefficient of a^d in zRow k f is [a^d z^k] f); the [z^0] is taken of the PRODUCT homfly (knotRestrict i) * homfly (knotRestrict j) in R, exactly as printed (excerpt 5, and the proof's point at 31-34), not of the factors separately. Quantifying over both orders (i, j) and (j, i) is equivalent to the printed labelled D_1 ∪ D_2 since mixedSignSum D i j = mixedSignSum D j i ({s,t} = {t,s} as a Finset, same crossing, same sign) and the product commutes.
